question: What Is Split Range Control?
body_html:
Split range control is a strategy where one controller output is divided so it drives two or more final control elements, each over its own part of the signal span.

A common split sends 4 to 12 mA to valve A and 12 to 20 mA to valve B. In a heating and cooling loop, the cooling valve works from 0% to 50% output while the heating valve opens from 50% to 100%.

It is used when one valve cannot cover the full range or two actions are needed.
